title: Azure SQL vs Cosmos DB
description: Compare Azure SQL Database and Cosmos DB across data models, consistency, pricing, and use cases to choose the right service.

data.text: Azure offers two very different database services: **Azure SQL Database** for relational, structured data with strong consistency, and **Cosmos DB** for globally distributed, schema-less NoSQL data with tunable consistency. Choosing the wrong service can lead to overpaying, poor performance, or unnecessary complexity.

data.title: Azure SQL Database vs Cosmos DB

cards.title: Azure SQL Database
cards.description: A fully managed relational database based on SQL Server.
pros: Mature ecosystem of tools and ORMs
cons: Limited global distribution compared to Cosmos DB
Scaling requires careful sharding for very large datasets
Higher latency for globally distributed reads

cards.title: Cosmos DB
cards.description: A globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database with tunable consistency.
pros: Multiple APIs (SQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table)
cons: NoSQL mindset required — no joins, no foreign keys
RU-based pricing is less predictable for new workloads
Query capabilities differ from relational SQL

rows: E-commerce product catalog with global users
Mobile app backend with variable traffic

terms.definition: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — the guarantees of a reliable transaction.
Cosmos DB's normalized throughput currency, distinct from SQL compute metrics.
A data model where each item can have different properties without schema migrations.

data.title: You Can Use Both
data.text: Many production apps use Azure SQL for transactional data and Cosmos DB for user profiles, catalogs, or telemetry. Choose the right tool for each job rather than forcing everything into one database.

data.title: Exercise: Architecture Decision Record
data.description: Choose a database service for a new application.
steps: Your team is building a global meal-delivery app with users, restaurants, menus, and orders.
For each entity group, decide between Azure SQL and Cosmos DB.
Write a short decision record explaining your reasoning for each choice.
Consider consistency, latency, query patterns, and cost.
data.expectedOutcome: A reasoned architecture decision record justifying database choices for each entity group.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure SQL is best for structured, relational data with strong consistency.
Cosmos DB excels at globally distributed, schema-less data with low latency.
Cost models differ: SQL charges for compute+storage; Cosmos DB charges for RUs+storage.
Many apps use both services together.
data.takeaway: There is no universal best database. Match the service to the data shape, consistency needs, and access patterns.
